contract.configuration: internal/command/entry.go render: SetEscapeHTML(false), compact JSON/JSONL, SetIndent("", "  ") for successful text result; exactly one trailing newline
contract.raw: RawValue remains borrowed. Duplicate fields, order, large integers, negative zero, exponent spelling, original string escapes, surrogate escape spellings and literal HTML/U+2028/U+2029 survive; remove only insignificant JSON whitespace. Pretty raw content participates in enclosing formatter indentation.
contract.typed: Normal strings retain PublicFormatter escaping, including U+2028/U+2029 escaping and literal HTML. Only actual f32/f64 serializer events use corresponding finite float formatting. Arbitrary_precision Number tokens and RawValue tokens are never coerced to binary64.
contract.preflight: Same deterministic Serialize value and format serializes to sink before output. Preflight validation errors emit no record. Second pass writes directly then newline; no Value conversion, full output buffer or report clone in encoder. Stable Serialize and already-compatible schema/key order/byte representation are producer requirements.
contract.io: Real writer errors and WriteZero map to external.io / exit 5 and may leave partial output. Formatter/raw serialization errors map to input.invalid / exit 4. Interrupted writes retry. There is no OS-atomic record guarantee.
contract.statefulSerialize: A custom serializer changing/failing between passes can leave partial output. This is documented and regression-covered; it is not concealed as an unconditional atomicity guarantee.
contract.limits: No public frame/report byte cap. Fixed Go MemoryMaxPayload = 512 << 10 (524288 bytes), enforced upstream for native reports. 8 << 20 is Rust journal checkpoint size, not report size. Raw validator/formatter use iterative stacks bounded by actual Go scanner maxNestingDepth=10000; compact RawMessage depth is independent, pretty final-document depth includes typed enclosing containers.
contract.performance: NOT_RUN. Two serialization passes, borrowed raw validation and iterative formatting have unmeasured CPU cost. No performance-target claim.
